about: Blind test reports for the report box: written WITHOUT looking at quickread.js, report.js or proxy/, so they test the readers instead of echoing them. 120 reports a panicking family member or neighbor might type or say during a search for a person with dementia near Fremont Central Park / Lake Elizabeth, in en/es/fr/zh/ja: typos, voice-transcription errors, panic, vague places, intersections, wrong-person sightings, jokes, car reports, water, searched-and-empty, questions. 'expect' is the correct ReportDraft reading: kind; place (a name from 'places', or null when no listed place fits and the person should tap the map); direction (8-point compass, or null when none is given; 'toward X' is null); minutes (for a sighting: minutes since seen, null if not said; for 'searched': minutes spent searching, if said; compare by bucket 0/5/10/15/30/60); reliability (sightings only: 0.3 maybe/far/second-hand, 0.6 plain or 'I think', 0.9 definitely; null otherwise). 'acceptable' lists other values per field that are not wrong. 'danger' is how bad acting on a WRONG reading of this report would be (high: could send volunteers the wrong way, mark an unsearched place cleared, pull the map onto a hazard or a stranger, or miss a car/water emergency; medium: misleads the map but self-corrects or adds mild false certainty; low: nothing to misread), and 'why' says how. Left empty (null) is always safer than a wrong value: an empty field goes to the person to fill in.

cases.text: saw dad by lake elizabeth maybe 10 min ago heading east, grey windbreaker
cases.why: A wrong place or direction moves the map and sends volunteers the wrong way. "maybe" hedges the time, not who it was.

cases.text: It was DEFINITELY her, I know my own mother. She was on Walnut Ave by the BART station going west 15 minutes ago
cases.why: A wrong place or direction moves the map; at 0.9 the wrong spot would dominate it.

cases.text: PLEASE HELP SHE'S GONE SHE WAS IN THE KITCHEN AND NOW SHES NOT HERE
cases.why: No place or sighting in it. Pinning it anywhere (e.g. the last-seen point as a fresh sighting) adds false certainty.

cases.text: corner of Paseo Padre and Walnut, guy at the gas station said an old man in slippers went by heading toward Stevenson about 20 min ago
cases.why: Second-hand: reading it as first-hand or certain over-weights a rumor.

cases.why: No usable place. Inventing one (or a high reliability) moves the map on nothing. No one says they saw anyone.

cases.text: someone on nextdoor posted they saw an old lady wandering around by the shopping area
cases.why: Second-hand: reading it as first-hand or certain over-weights a rumor. "the shopping area" is not on the list; leave the pin to the person.

cases.text: maybe aliens took him haha. seriously tho nobody has seen him since lunch
cases.why: A joke. Any pin or sighting from it is invented.

cases.text: his car is gone too, we think he drove somewhere maybe 40 min ago
cases.why: Driving changes everything: the walking model is wrong, police need the plate now. Read as a foot sighting, the map stays on a small walking area while the person is miles away.

cases.text: found her shoe on the path by lake elizabeth, right by the water. i think she went in. CALLING 911
cases.why: Physical evidence at the water: missing the place or reading it as a worry delays a water search where minutes matter.

cases.text: what if he fell in the creek?? there's that creek near laguna
cases.why: A worry, not a sighting. Pinning it to the water as a sighting pulls volunteers to a hazard on a guess (the water should be checked by professionals, not because of this pin).

cases.text: spent like 45 min going around lake elizabeth, the full loop, no sign of her
cases.why: Read as a sighting, it would pull the map INTO an area just found empty, the opposite of the truth.

cases.text: we did the north side of the lake but not the south side yet
cases.why: Only part was searched. Marking the whole place as searched lowers the unsearched half too.

cases.text: should we look in the creek or wait for police?
cases.why: A question. Read as "searched", it would mark a place cleared that nobody checked — the most dangerous misread.

cases.text: where do I go?? I'm at the library parking lot
cases.why: The reporter's own location, not a sighting. Pinned as a sighting it pulls the map to the library.

cases.text: she's not at the senior center on Liberty, I called them
cases.why: Only a phone call to a building. Marking the street as searched lowers an area no one walked.

cases.text: i saw her on Paseo padre parkway going north hey Siri stop ten minutes ago
cases.why: A wrong place or direction moves the map and sends volunteers the wrong way. "hey Siri stop" is noise.

cases.text: saw him around 3:15 by city hall on liberty st heading east
cases.why: Clock time, not "minutes ago". Guessing a number of minutes without knowing the current time can be far off.

cases.text: might have been him?? far away, across the lake on the other side, couldnt tell. just now
cases.why: Reading this far, uncertain sighting as definite (0.9) would pull the whole map onto one glimpse.
